messages:
deploy-bot: Started staged rollout v2026.03.17-rc2 -> canary (10% traffic). Build: inf-runtime-20260317. Cmd: `./deploy --staged --policy=canary` :rocket:
jin: seeing p99 jump on canary within 60s of rollout, from ~120ms -> ~1.3s. Throughput dropped ~18%. Logs show a burst of kernel_fallback events.
samir: paging oncall :rotating_light: metrics look bad, can you paste the dashboard link?
jin: https://grafana.redwood/board/rl-runtime?panel=latency-canary p95/p99 spikes. error rate from 0.8% -> 4.9%.
incident-bot: Paging on-call team: latency spike + kernel fallback on canary (p99>1s, errors up). Incident created INC-2026-1034.
nina: I see a new prefetch patch flipped in this release (preload_kv=true) that may be triggering fallback under certain sequence lengths. Reverting flag for canary now. CMD: `./flags set --env=canary preload_kv=false`
deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: preload_kv=false for canary.
lars: kernel_fallback counter still climbing, but CPU avg on node pool increased too. Might be a hot loop in prefetch path.
jin: paste logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:01Z] runtime: kv_prefetch: seq_len=2048, mem_est=1.2GB, try_prefetch -> fallback_kernel path
[2026-03-17T14:02:01Z] runtime: kernel_fallback++ name=prefetch_overrun node=gpupool-12
[2026-03-17T14:02:02Z] rpc: request latency=1203ms route=/redwood.generate model=gpt-open-7b
```
ops-runner: Customer impact: CS reports 3 enterprise tenants saw elevated tail latencies and some 502s for ~2m while canary was at 10% traffic. No broad outage yet.
samir: ok plan: 1) keep flag off on canary and monitor 2) if p99 doesn't start normalizing in 3m, initiate canary rollback to previous stable build and flip kill-switch for rollout 3) notify sales/customer-ops.
nina: toggled preload_kv off globally for canary. Also enabling extra logging for kernel_fallback to gather counts. CMD: `./infractl metrics annotate --tag=INC-2026-1034`
lars: after flag toggle CPU on canary nodes trending down, p99 decreasing to ~350ms now. error rate down to 1.2%.
jin: good signal. I'm holding off rollback for now but ready. Samir, can you open a rollback window just in case?
samir: opened rollback window and put auto-kill flag on the staged rollout. CMD: `./deploy rollback-window --id=v2026.03.17-rc2 --duration=15m`
incident-bot: Auto-kill policy armed for release v2026.03.17-rc2: will stop if error_rate>3% or p99>1s for 5m.
ops-runner: CS notified customers A/B/C with a short heads-up. Engineering oncall is coordinating with CS for post-incident notes.
jin: quick postmortem notes: root cause likely regression in prefetch kernel path under long sequences causing kernel_fallback thrash + batcher contention -> rising latency. Fix options: revert prefetch change, add defensive backoff in prefetch, improve estimation to avoid fallback.
oncall-next: taking handoff. I'm here for the next 60m. Will keep dashboard up, watching p99, kernel_fallback, and batch queue length. Link to runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/incident/runtime-kernel-fallback
lars: can we add temporary traffic-slice isolation to prevent cascade to other pools? I can spin a slice with prefetch disabled and shift canary traffic there.
samir: go for it, lars. Do it as a containment step if tests hold.
jin: confirmed p99 back to baseline ~140ms after the toggle and no more 502 reports. I'll keep the incident open until we validate full rollback or a code fix.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1034 updated: status=investigating -> mitigated (canary stabilized).
ops-runner: drafting incident note for CS and Exec. Will attach timeline and affected tenants.
oncall-next: ack, will follow up with a detailed timeline and handoff to next shift. :white_check_mark:
